raj: Hey team - getting reports from multiple customers (corp-acme, finco) where GitHub SSO fails with an 'invalid_state' / 'PKCE mismatch' right after redirect. Only repros when a tracking query param is present (utm_source).

jessica: Can you share a repro + any session ids? Which env (prod/stage)? :thinking:

raj: Prod. Quick repro steps below - seen from a user behind our CDN+link-tracker. Session id: sess_7a9f.
```
# reproduce (example)
curl -v "https://login.redwood.example.com/callback?utm_source=newsletter&code=OAUTH_CODE_ABC123&state=st_random_42" -H "Host: app.redwood.example.com"
# response Location header we got from upstream auth provider (GitHub):
# Location: https://login.redwood.example.com/callback?utm_source=newsletter&code=OAUTH_CODE_ABC123&state=st_random_42
```

mike: Hmm. The auth handler should parse `state` by name. Do you have the auth-service logs around the handshake? My suspicion: our edge router canonicalizes/normalizes query strings (alphabetical reorder) for cache keys, and some older client code we're using to parse the callback reads params positionally (bug).

raj: Paste from auth logs (redacted):
```
[2026-03-15T12:02:33Z] auth.oauth: incoming callback from github; raw_query="utm_source=newsletter&code=OAUTH_CODE_ABC123&state=st_random_42"
[2026-03-15T12:02:33Z] auth.oauth: parsed_query=["code","state","utm_source"] // ???
[2026-03-15T12:02:33Z] auth.oauth: state_received="st_random_42" expected="st_random_42"
[2026-03-15T12:02:33Z] auth.oauth: pkce_verifier_missing=true, reject invalid_grant
[2026-03-15T12:02:33Z] auth.oauth: responding 400 invalid_grant
```

jessica: So logs show state present but verifier missing. Is the code_verifier being sent in the same redirect? Typically PKCE is sent by the client (stored at login time). Could the router be stripping a fragment or cookie used to validate?

mike: Two possible issues:
1) Our login flow relies on a session cookie created on the initial /authorize request. If the CDN rewrites the redirect to include utm params and marks it cacheable, the cookie might not be attached on the returned request, so server can't find code_verifier.
2) The parsing lib we use (old-query) has a bug when query order is mutated while URL has tracking params. It ends up mapping keys incorrectly into array indices. We should never rely on order - fix lib or replace parse call with standard net/url parsing.

raj: Quick curl that reproduces the failure when the CDN adds utm param AFTER the provider redirect (mimics link shortener):
```
# original redirect from GH -> our callback
https://login.redwood.example.com/callback?code=OAUTH_CODE_ABC123&state=st_random_42
# proxy rewrites -> adds utm and reorders
https://login.redwood.example.com/callback?utm_source=newsletter&code=OAUTH_CODE_ABC123&state=st_random_42
# result: session cookie not present (edge cached) so pkce_verifier not found -> invalid_grant
```

lara: Assigning to eng-platform. Escalating: affects >5 customers, auth SLO bleeding. support-bot: create ticket and link customers.

support-bot: created TICKET-13287 and linked sessions [sess_7a9f, sess_8b2c]. Owners: @mike, @lara. Priority: P1. :rotating_light:

mike: Short-term mitigations:
- Update auth-service to robustly load `state` and `code` by key (not index) and fallback to reading PKCE from a signed state payload.
- Configure CDN: stop canonicalizing query string for /callback endpoints (preserve order and pass-through cookies). I can put a no-cache rule for that path.
- Add logging: metric auth.state_missing and auth.pkce_missing with tags:cdn=true/false, has_utm=true/false.
I'll open a PR for the auth handler patch now.

jessica: Please paste the PR and ETA. Also ping customer success for impacted accounts so they know the timeline.

mike: PR: github.com/redwood/auth-service/pull/248 (fix: parse by key + pkce fallback). ETA 2h for canary, 6h for full rollout if smoke passes. CDN rule change in 30m (config only).

lara: We'll run a canary in prod with 10% traffic to auth-service and monitor auth.* metrics + error budget. If green, roll to 100% in 3 hours. Also add an integration test that replays redirect with extra utm params.

raj: Thanks — I pushed a tiny repro harness to test org and confirmed the canary bypasses the error when using patched auth-build. Will follow up after canary.

lara: Canary done: metrics look good, auth.invalid_grant down to baseline. Deploying to full in 15m.

raj: Confirmed with corp-acme user: login succeeded. Closing this thread. :white_check_mark:
